resources.string: Keeping the host connection and playback alive

Cannot reach the host. Is it running in Termux? If it was, the system may have frozen Termux in the background: switch to Termux and back, then retry. Lock Termux in recents and set its battery usage to unrestricted.
The reverse proxy rejected the username/password. Check them, then reconnect.
The proxy wants you to sign in first (it redirects to %1$s). Open that address in a browser, sign in there, then retry.
Proxy sign-in did not take effect after several attempts. Check the username/password, then reconnect manually.
Proxy session expired. Signing in again…

The server\'s TLS certificate could not be verified (not issued by a trusted CA), or the handshake was cut. For a private CA: install that root CA on the phone under Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate — the app trusts user-installed CAs, like a browser does.
Cannot resolve the host name. Check the address for typos, and your DNS/network.
Timed out connecting to the host. Check the address, the port, and your network.
Cannot reach the host port (refused, or blocked by a firewall). Check the address, the port, and that the host service is running.
Cannot reach the host. Check the address, the port, and that the service is running, then retry.
The server requires a client certificate (mTLS). If you dismissed the system certificate picker, reconnect and pick one; if you have none, install a client certificate on the phone first.

%1$s has a TLS certificate problem:
%2$s

A browser may open it while this app cannot, because Chrome uses its own certificate verifier, not the one this app uses. Only choose “Connect anyway” if you are sure this is your own server.
